featured_reviews.name: Swad Stories
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Govinda's Restaurant near Chowpatty, Girgaon, and had a wonderful dining experience. What makes this place truly unique is that, being associated with the ISKCON Temple Trust, they do not use garlic or onions in any of their preparations. Despite this, the food is incredibly flavorful and satisfying, proving that great taste doesn't always need conventional ingredients.

The menu offers a wide variety of options across different cuisines. We started our meal with a selection of soups including Artichoke Bisque, Minestrone, Manchow, Tomato Lemongrass, and Laksa Soup. Each soup had a distinct flavor profile and was perfectly balanced. My personal favorite was the Artichoke Bisque Soup, as it was my first time trying it and I absolutely loved its rich, creamy texture and unique taste.

For starters, we ordered the Kung Pao Paneer and Masala Papad. The paneer was well-cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the masala papad made for a light and crunchy accompaniment.

In the main course, we enjoyed Paneer Lababdar and Dal Tadka paired with Jeera Rice. The gravies were comforting, flavorful, and complemented the rice beautifully.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Sizzling Brownie. Served hot and indulgent, it was the perfect way to end the dining experience.

Overall, Govinda's is a small yet charming restaurant with a constant flow of patrons, which speaks volumes about its popularity. If you're looking for delicious vegetarian food with a unique sattvic approach, this place is definitely worth a visit.

WAH 🚀! Just had an UNEXPECTEDLY EPIC meal at the Govinda's - didn't know food could vibe with divinity like this 🪔🍴!

🔹 *Benne Dosa*: Soft, buttery, South Indian heaven!. The benne (butter) was rich and aromatic - loved it!
🔹 *Farm Fresh Pizza*: Wait, a farm-fresh pizza inside a temple? 🤯! Toppings were fresh, crust was spot on 🍕. Got the vibe that the ingredients were picked fresh for the temple devotees... felt special!

Eating amidst the temple's vibes, felt like a foodie blessing 🙌. Service was super attentive 😊.

If you're around Iskon anywhere in the world, Govinda's is an absolute MUST 📍. Blend of divine vibes + tasty food = recipe for a soulful meal 👌."

featured_reviews.review_text:
Review: Soam Restaurant, Mumbai

We stay in Chembur and our family visited Soam restaurant in SoBo for the first time and enjoyed a truly satisfying vegetarian dining experience.

We ordered a wide spread of dishes — panki, sev puri, dahi puri, dahi bhalla chaat, watana ghughra, sada dosa, aloo puri with potato subji, thepla with red potato subji, moong dal khichadi and kadhi. Each item was flavorful, well‑prepared, and appreciated by everyone at the table.

The service was prompt and courteous, making the meal smooth and enjoyable. The atmosphere was decent, not extraordinary, but comfortable enough for a relaxed family outing.

One point worth noting is the pricing. Compared to similar restaurants in the suburbs, Soam is on the higher side. Perhaps this is the premium for being a very popular SoBo (South Bombay) restaurant.

Overall, Soam impressed us with its authentic flavors and variety. It’s a place we would recommend to anyone looking for wholesome vegetarian food in South Mumbai, while keeping in mind the pricing.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Gujarati feast with a seasonal twist, Gujju Bhai No Thali is absolutely worth a visit right now!

The highlight of the experience is their unlimited aamras, served fresh as a summer special—and honestly, it steals the show. Sweet, rich, and perfectly chilled, it pairs beautifully with their hot, fluffy puris… pure comfort on a plate.

The thali itself is incredibly wholesome and satisfying. It starts off with refreshing drinks like chaas and pudina pani, setting the tone for what’s to come. The appetisers—kachori, dhokla, and chaat tart—are all fresh and flavourful, giving you that perfect mix of crunch, spice, and tang.

Moving to the mains, you’re treated to four different sabjis, two dals, and a classic Gujarati kadhi that strikes the perfect balance of sweet and tangy. Pair these with soft phulkas or puris, and it’s a complete meal in itself. You also get options like jeera rice and comforting dal khichdi, which just add to the homely feel of the meal.

And just when you think you’re done, the desserts keep coming! From warm halwa to the indulgent malai sandwich, everything feels like a celebration of flavours.

Overall, Gujju Bhai No Thali delivers a hearty, value-for-money dining experience with that signature Gujarati hospitality. With the mango season in full swing, the unlimited aamras makes it even more special—definitely not to be missed!

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

I recently visited Flute Restaurant inside Krishna Palace Hotel at Grant Road for lunch along with a colleague, and the experience was delightful from start to finish. The ambience is classy yet comfortable, with a touch of elegance that makes it perfect for both business and casual outings.

We started with Chicken Manchow Soup, Dynamite Prawns, and a refreshing Watermelon Salad, all of which set a great tone for the meal. The Mumbai Sunshine cocktail was vibrant and well-balanced.

For the mains, we had Chicken Lehsuni, Bhatti Da Murg, and Cheese Garlic Naan – the Lehsuni Chicken was undoubtedly the star of the show with its bold, garlicky taste. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
An unforgettable Thai brunch experience that truly transported us straight to the bustling streets of Bangkok 🇹🇭✨
We recently attended the Tuk Tuk Tales pop-up at Plate & Pint curated by the incredibly talented Chef Akanksha Saigal, and every single dish on the menu reflected her passion, creativity, and deep understanding of authentic Thai flavours.
We went as a group of friends for brunch, and honestly, it turned into one of those meals where every plate sparks conversation, every bite feels memorable, and time just flies by over great food and even better company. The vibe at Plate & Pint added so much warmth to the experience — lively, cozy, vibrant, and perfect for a long indulgent afternoon.
The meal began with the Mango & Avocado Ceviche — incredibly fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced with chilli, lime, cilantro, green apple, and crispy shallots adding layers of texture and zing. A refreshing start that instantly awakened the palate.
The Crispy Potato Stacks were an absolute standout. Perfectly crisp with rich green curry notes, aromatic fried basil, chilli crackling, and toasted herb rice bringing together comfort and complexity in every bite.
The Gai Yang Thai BBQ Chicken was beautifully charred and deeply flavourful, paired wonderfully with pickled cucumber, pickled chilli, and a delicious dipping sauce that elevated the smokiness of the chicken.
The Spicy Tamarind Glaze dishes were another highlight. Both the cottage cheese and pork belly versions were packed with bold sweet spicy flavours and had that addictive Thai style balance that keeps you reaching for another bite.
For mains, the Holy Basil Stir Fry was pure comfort food done right. Fragrant basil, juicy chicken, cucumber, fluffy rice, and a fried egg made this dish hearty, satisfying, and incredibly soulful.
The Tom Yum Hot Pot was bursting with authentic Thai aromatics — lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf — with the prawns soaking beautifully in the deeply comforting broth. Warm, sharp, spicy, and layered with flavour.
And of course, no Thai meal feels complete without a great Pad Thai, and this one absolutely delivered. Perfectly cooked rice noodles coated in tamarind sauce with chicken, bean sprouts, and peanuts creating the ideal balance of sweet, savoury, nutty, and tangy flavours.
Dessert was the perfect finale — Mango Sticky Rice with tender coconut ice cream. Rich, fragrant, comforting, and tropical all at once. Easily one of the best versions we’ve had in Mumbai.
The cocktails were equally thoughtful and fun, especially the Thai Chilli Guava Michelada and Mango Chilli White Wine Spritz, which paired beautifully with the food and added another vibrant layer to the entire experience.
Huge compliments to Chef Akanksha for creating such a well executed pop-up that didn’t just serve food, but genuinely told a story through flavours. Every dish felt curated with heart and authenticity.
Thank you for inviting us and giving us such a memorable afternoon filled with laughter, amazing conversations, delicious food, and beautiful hospitality. Experiences like these are exactly why food brings people together so effortlessly.

Already looking forward to the next one ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
Revival is one of those places that quietly delivers on everything you expect from a comforting dining experience. With its sea facing setting and focus on Pure Veg and Jain food, it is a spot that naturally lends itself to relaxed family outings.

A recent visit was centred around their Summer Special Mango Menu, which brings in a refreshing seasonal touch. The Kairi Kanda Roomali and Pakoda made for a great start and disappeared almost instantly. The Paneer Kairi Tikka stood out with its soft texture and well balanced flavours, easily one of the highlights from the menu.

The beverage selection complements the theme well. Options like the Mango Frozen Margarita and Mango Passion Fruit Mojito are refreshing, while the Mango Lassi is a great pick if you are in the mood for something richer and more filling.

Moving to the mains, the Paneer Khada Masala with Garlic leaves a strong impression and ranks among the better versions you will come across. It fits perfectly into the kind of comforting, flavourful food this place is known for.

Desserts keep things traditional and satisfying. The Gulab Jamun paired with Lacchedar Rabdi works beautifully, while the Aamras Puri is an easy choice, especially during the season.

What makes Revival stand out is how easy it is to return to. It is the kind of place that works just as well for a casual meal as it does for a family outing, and even welcomes your furry companions.

Conveniently located a short walk from Charni Road station, and set within a heritage building just off the Chowpatty seaface, it is a spot that is both accessible and consistently dependable when you are in the mood for good, comforting food.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for your wonderful 5-star review! We’re glad you had such a comforting and memorable dining experience — looking forward to welcoming you again soon.

featured_reviews.review_text: Had a really good vegetarian meal after a long time. Definitely satisfied my craving for Indian food. And the vibe is just perfect with the spectacular sea view. I personally loved the Bharwan Mirch, Mega Naan, and Alag Khichdi, but everything I tried was top-tier.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Nayan Bheda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience on Diwali
We were a group of 5 who had booked a table a day in advance through Google for 20th Oct, 9pm. On calling the restaurant in the afternoon about parking, the manager suddenly claimed they have “stopped online reservations” — even though the slot was available and confirmed on Google. When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. The high-handed attitude spoiled our mood. Especially when the prices are comparable with premium restaurants. While prices match that of premium restaurant, the customer-centric attitude does not.

Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

Overall, good food and smiling service of Kabir the waiter saved complete disaster. One star is for him. 4 stars goes out for an unprofessional and disappointing handling of guests. Would not recommend until management fixes confirmed reservations, billing transparency and how they treat their customers.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for sharing your detailed feedback. We sincerely apologize for the issues you faced with reservations, billing, and management, and will take steps to improve our service and guest experience.

The ambience is absolutely refreshing, especially with its beautiful sea-facing view that makes the entire meal feel relaxing and special. The restaurant is well-suited for families, couples, and even pet owners, which adds a unique and welcoming touch.

The pure vegetarian and Jain food options are thoughtfully prepared, fresh, and full of flavor. Every dish feels hygienic and light, yet satisfying. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures a smooth dining experience from start to finish.

Overall, it’s a perfect place to enjoy peaceful meals with great views, good service, and a warm atmosphere. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a clean, serene, and enjoyable vegetarian dining spot.

featured_reviews.name: Shubham Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Crystal Restaurant at Chowpatty is one of those classic places in Mumbai that has built its reputation over many years by serving consistently good food. Located close to the famous Girgaon Chowpatty, it’s a convenient spot to visit after enjoying the sea breeze or an evening walk on the beach.

The restaurant is known mainly for its simple yet delicious North Indian and vegetarian dishes. Their Punjabi thali, dal makhani, paneer preparations, and butter rotis are especially popular among regular customers. The food is rich in flavor, well-cooked, and feels like traditional home-style North Indian cuisine. Portion sizes are also quite generous, making it a good value-for-money place, especially if you’re dining with family.

One thing that stands out about Crystal is its old-school charm. The interiors are simple and not overly fancy, but the place has a warm and nostalgic feel that many longtime visitors appreciate. The staff is generally polite and efficient, and even during busy hours they try their best to serve quickly.

Another positive point is the location. Being so close to Chowpatty makes it a great stop for a proper meal after having street food or spending time by the beach. Many locals and tourists visit this restaurant when they want something more filling than snacks.

However, during peak hours the place can get quite crowded, and you might have to wait for a table. The ambiance is also more traditional than modern, so those expecting a luxury dining experience might find it a bit basic.

Overall, Crystal Restaurant is a reliable place for tasty North Indian vegetarian food in the Chowpatty area. If you’re looking for comforting meals, generous portions, and a classic Mumbai dining experience, it’s definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to experience old-school Mumbai charm with soulful food and timeless vibes, then Crystal Restaurant Chowpatty is a place you simply cannot miss. Located exactly opposite Girgaon Chowpatty near Wilson College, this iconic decade-old restaurant carries the true essence of vintage Mumbai. The moment you walk in, it feels like stepping into a different era — simple interiors, retro atmosphere, classic old Hindi songs playing softly in the background, and that comforting feeling modern cafés often fail to give.
What makes this place special is not fancy presentation or luxury décor, but the authenticity. The vibe here is peaceful, nostalgic, and beautifully old-fashioned. Perfect spot after a long Marine Drive walk or a relaxed dinner with family and friends. The combination of Chowpatty breeze, retro Bollywood music, and homely Punjabi-style food creates an experience that feels warm and memorable.

What makes this place special is not fancy presentation or luxury décor, but the authenticity. The vibe here is peaceful, nostalgic, and beautifully old-fashioned. The ghee chapati, paneer dishes, rajma chawal, dal tadka, parathas, and especially the famous rice kheer are absolutely worth trying. Peri Peri Prawns – Prawns batter fried and tossed in peri peri sauce along with a few cubes of mix peppers. Loved the crunchiness of the prawns and the sauce was coated so well. (5/5)

Mutton Rogan josh – A classical dish made in the most authentic way. Boneless mutton cubes cooked so well in thin traditional rogan josh gravy. The Doneness of the mutton was too good. I had garlic butter naan with it, which was just perfect. (5/5)
